finalResponse:
# Global Compensation Policy Redesign — Remote Company, 30 Countries

## 1. Diagnose before designing: three problems are being conflated

| Symptom | Actual root cause | Wrong fix |
|---|---|---|
| Warsaw/Lisbon engineers comparing to Berlin/Toronto on forums | The **spread is too wide** (likely 2.0–2.5× between top and bottom zones) and the **rationale is undocumented**, so gaps read as arbitrary rather than principled | Telling people not to discuss pay (illegal in most of these jurisdictions, and futile) |
| Benchmark data no longer supports 30 discrete country bands | **Too much granularity** — thin survey samples in small markets produce noisy, unstable, unexplainable numbers | Buying more data |
| Transparency laws expose internal gaps | Gaps that were **tolerable when invisible are not defensible when visible** — including gaps you can't explain with objective criteria | Minimum-compliance disclosure |

The strategic point: transparency doesn't create pay problems, it removes the option of not resolving them. Design for the world where every number is public, because by 2027 it effectively is.

---

## 2. Five design principles

1. **Pay for the role and the level, not the person's postcode.** Location is a *bounded modifier*, not the primary determinant.
2. **Fewer, broader, more defensible units.** Zones beat countries; job families beat job titles.
3. **Every pay difference must survive the "explain it in one sentence to the affected employee" test.** If it can't, it's an exception, and exceptions get a budget and an expiry date.
4. **Global elements where you can, local elements where you must.** Equity and bonus targets equalize; cash localizes.
5. **Publish the method, not just the minimum.** Methodology transparency buys credibility that outcome transparency alone destroys.

---

## 3. The architecture

### 3.1 Global job architecture (foundation — do this first)
A single levelling framework across all 30 countries: job families (Engineering, Product, GTM, G&A), levels (e.g., IC1–IC8, M1–M5), with written scope/impact/autonomy criteria per level. Every employee mapped, every mapping reviewed by a calibration panel.

This is also the **legal spine**: the EU Pay Transparency Directive requires employers to define categories of workers performing "work of equal value" using objective, gender-neutral criteria. If you don't define those categories, an employee's lawyer will — and they'll pick the grouping that maximizes the gap.

### 3.2 A single global reference market
Price every level once, against one anchor market (recommend a blended US Tier-1 or a Zone-1 composite), from named sources (e.g., Radford/Pave for tech, Figures or WTW for EU markets). This produces one number per level: the **global reference midpoint**.

### 3.3 Compressed geographic zones (4–5, not 30)

| Zone | Illustrative locations | Multiplier of reference |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | SF Bay, NYC, Seattle, Zurich | 1.00 |
| 2 | Toronto, Berlin, Amsterdam, London, Dublin, Sydney | 0.82 |
| 3 | Lisbon, Madrid, Warsaw, Kraków, Prague, Montreal | 0.68 |
| 4 | Bucharest, Belgrade, Mexico City, São Paulo, Bengaluru | 0.55 |

**Floor rule: no zone below 0.50 of reference.** The compression is the core intervention. If the old model had Warsaw at ~0.45 and Berlin at ~0.85, a Warsaw engineer saw a 47% discount; at 0.68 vs 0.82 it's 17% — a gap that a rational person can accept as "cost-of-labor plus local market reality" rather than "I'm a cheaper body doing identical work."

Zone assignment rule, published: zones are set by a composite of (a) market pay data for software roles, (b) employer competitive set, (c) statutory cost loading — **not** by cost of living. Cost-of-living framing is indefensible the moment someone points out that groceries in Zurich cost 2× Warsaw but not 3×, and it invites the question "why do you care what my rent is?" Cost of *labor* is a market fact; cost of living is a judgement about how employees should live.

### 3.4 Band structure
- Each level × zone = one band, width ~80–120% of the zone midpoint (narrower at senior levels).
- Position in band driven by *documented* criteria only: performance rating, time in level, scarce-skill premium (defined list, reviewed annually), and manager discretion capped at ±5% with written justification.
- **Publish the full grid internally**, plus an employee-facing calculator: select level and location → see the band. This kills the forum problem, because the forum can only reveal what you've already published.

### 3.5 Globalize the non-cash elements
- **Equity: identical grant value for identical level, worldwide.** No geo multiplier. This is the single most powerful fairness lever — it says ownership of the company is not location-dependent — and it's cheap in cash terms.
- **Bonus targets: identical % of salary by level, worldwide.**
- **Benefits: a global minimum standard** (parental leave floor, health/wellness stipend, home-office budget, learning budget) topped up locally to statutory requirements — never down.

Result: total-comp spread across zones narrows further than cash spread. A Zone-3 engineer at IC5 might be at 0.68 on salary but 0.78 on total comp.

### 3.6 Movement and mobility rules (pre-decide these)
- Move to a higher zone: adjusted up at next cycle.
- Move to a lower zone: **12-month protection**, then adjusted down to the new zone maximum for the level — never below. Publish this before anyone moves.
- Zone reassignment of a *city* (market shifts): only upward for incumbents; new hires priced at the new zone.
- No salary-history questions anywhere (already illegal in much of the EU under the Directive and in many US states — make it a global policy to avoid importing old inequities).

---

## 4. Transparency and compliance layer

**Compliance floor (must-do by jurisdiction):**
- Pay ranges in job postings — EU (Directive, transposition due June 2026), plus CO, CA, NY, WA, IL, HI, and others. **Simplify: post ranges on every requisition globally.** Maintaining 30 different posting rules is more expensive than universal disclosure.
- Employee right to request average pay for their category, broken down by sex — build a self-service report, don't handle these ad hoc.
- Gender pay gap reporting (EU: phased from 2027 by headcount; also UK, Ireland, Spain, France's Index Égalité).
- Joint pay assessment trigger if an unexplained gap >5% persists in any category — **run this analysis privately now**, before the obligation bites.

**The sharp legal risk nobody flags early:** if your lower-paid zones happen to skew female (or by any protected characteristic), location-based pay becomes potential *indirect discrimination*, and "the market is cheaper there" may not qualify as an objective justification under EU law. Run a regression of pay on level, zone, tenure, performance, and sex/other protected traits across the whole workforce. If zone correlates with gender composition, you either raise the floor faster or you have a live exposure.

**Voluntary transparency (do more than required):** publish internally the zone list, the multipliers, the data sources, the review cadence, and the promotion criteria per level. Publish externally the *methodology* (not individual data). Candidates and employees forgive a lower number far more readily than an unexplained one.

---

## 5. Transition plan

**Phase 0 (months 1–2):** Job architecture build + level mapping + full pay-equity regression. No announcements.

**Phase 1 (month 3):** Model the cost. Compressing the bottom typically costs **2–5% of global payroll**; validate against your actual distribution. Fund it from: reduced Zone-1 hiring mix, reduced attrition-and-replacement cost (a regretted senior engineer costs 6–12 months of salary), and one cycle of moderated top-of-band increases in Zone 1.

**Phase 2 (month 4):** Announce the *framework* before the *numbers*. Explain the shift from 30 country bands to zones, the compression, the equity equalization, and the mobility rules.

**Phase 3 (months 5–7):** Individual adjustments in a single global cycle.
- **No pay cuts. Ever, in this transition.** Anyone above the new band is red-circled: salary held, future increases delivered as bonus/equity until the band catches up.
- Below-band employees brought to minimum immediately; two tranches only if cost forces it, with both dates communicated up front.

**Phase 4 (ongoing):** Annual refresh, single global effective date, published calendar.

---

## 6. Governance and metrics

**Governance:** a Compensation Committee (CPO, CFO, Chief Legal, one engineering leader) owns zone assignments and the annual multiplier refresh. Multipliers change at most once a year, by no more than 5 points, with published rationale. Exception rate hard-capped at 5% of offers, tracked by manager.

**FX and inflation:** salaries denominated in local currency; automatic review trigger if FX moves >10% against the anchor currency; off-cycle mechanism for high-inflation markets (Turkey, Argentina, Egypt) using a published index rather than negotiation.

**Metrics reviewed quarterly:**
- Unexplained pay gap by category (target: <5%, the joint-assessment trigger)
- Compa-ratio distribution by zone, level, gender, ethnicity where lawfully collected
- Regretted attrition by zone (the real signal that a multiplier is too low)
- Offer acceptance rate and time-to-fill by zone
- Exception rate and out-of-band population
- Internal-equity pulse: "I understand how my pay is set" and "I believe my pay is fair relative to colleagues" — track the *understanding* score separately, because it's the one you can move fastest

---

## 7. Pre-decided answers to the hard questions

| Question you will be asked | Answer |
|---|---|
| "Why do I earn less than Berlin for the same work?" | "Your zone multiplier is 0.68 vs 0.82, set from these named market sources, reviewed annually, published in full. Your equity and bonus target are identical to Berlin's." |
| "So pay me the Berlin rate." | Single global rate = ~15–25% payroll increase and effectively ends hiring outside high-cost markets. We compress the gap instead of eliminating it. |
| "Can I move to Bali and keep my salary?" | No — published mobility rules, plus tax/permanent-establishment constraints. Approved country list only. |
| "You're cutting Zone-1 pay to fund this." | No cuts. Zone-1 growth moderates for one cycle. |
| "Will you publish individual salaries?" | No. We publish bands, methodology, and aggregate gaps. Individual pay stays confidential; employees remain free to disclose their own. |

**The core trade being made:** a few points of payroll cost, spent to buy explainability. In a transparent-pay world, the return on a defensible system is realized in retention and hiring speed in exactly the markets — Warsaw, Lisbon, Kraków — where the current model is quietly bleeding senior talent to competitors who have already made this move.
